claims.label: Alleged university announcement
claims.text: “Management has suspended all lectures on Monday because of a security situation. Sources in the admin office say. Share urgently!”
claims.explain: This could be true or false. There is no named source or official notice, so do not believe or share it yet. Investigate: check the official university channels, ask your department or course rep, and wait for confirmation.

claims.label: Viral scholarship opportunity
claims.text: “FREE ₦500,000 for every Nigerian student! Share this message with 10 groups to qualify.”
claims.explain: Reject it. Real scholarships do not require you to forward messages, and they name a provider. This is a chain message built to spread.

claims.label: Forwarded health claim
claims.text: “Doctors confirm hot lemon water cures malaria. No need to go to hospital. Forward to save lives.”
claims.explain: Reject it. No named doctor or study, and malaria needs proper testing and treatment. Sharing it could lead someone to delay care. If unsure, ask a pharmacist or clinic.

claims.label: Suspicious news headline
claims.source: Unknown site, no author or date
claims.text: “BREAKING: Government to ban phones on all campuses from January, says anonymous insider.”
claims.explain: Plausible-sounding but weak: no author, date or named source. Investigate: find the original source and see whether reliable outlets or official statements report it independently.

claims.label: Image with a misleading caption
claims.text: A photo of a flooded street captioned “Akure flood today!!” A commenter says the same photo appeared in a news story three years ago about another city.
claims.explain: Reject it as captioned. The comment is checkable: a reverse image search shows where and when the photo first appeared. Do not share it with that caption.
